name: One Meridian Plaza highrise office fire
source: USFA-TR-049 (see sources.md); page numbers are the report's printed pages

t0.meaning: first smoke detector activation on the 22nd floor; the report says the fire was already well advanced (room of origin flashed over) by then, so minute 0 is DETECTION, not ignition. Ignition time is unknown (rags left unattended over the weekend).

$tickNote: one simulation tick = 4 minutes (calibration, step 3): a space's fuel burns for 50 ticks = 200 min, and the floor-to-floor milestones fit the report; see plan.spec.json $calibration

stairs.note: in the core, west end; door on 22 locked at arrival
in the core; Engine 11 went up this stair
east end, connects to the attached Girard Trust Building

elevatorBanks.note: two shafts, six passenger cars; one freight car serves 22-38

building.returnAirShafts: one at each of the four corners, no fire dampers

convenienceStair.note: open interior stair; fire dropped to 21 through it

electricalRoom.note: both commercial feeds in one enclosure; fire here caused the total power failure

building.detectors: smoke detectors at exit access points, return-air intakes at the four corners, elevator lobbies and corridors (1981 amendments); open-plan floors only at the exits; manual pull stations at each stair on every floor
building.fuel: files and papers (securities trading, management consulting); one floor with heavy computer/electronic load

ignition.detectorHint: the activated detector is believed to be at the northeast return-air shaft intake

events.text: Smoke detector on 22 activates; alarm sounds; elevators recall. Room of origin already flashed over.

Building engineer overrides recall and rides to 22; heavy smoke and heat; trapped in the car; recalled by the lobby guard. Alarm company phones the lobby, is told it is being checked; nobody calls the fire department.
Passer-by 9-1-1 call in progress; alarm monitoring service reports the fire. First alarm dispatched: 4 engines, 2 ladders, 2 battalion chiefs.
Engine 43 on scene: heavy smoke, fire from one window at mid-height. Security guard tells the battalion chief: 22nd floor.
Incident commander knows the fire floor (22) from the guard and one window.
Second alarm.
Attack team takes the low-rise elevators to 11 and walks up; lobby command post.
Total electrical power failure (fire penetrates the 22nd-floor electrical room; both feeds short; generator fails). No lights, no elevators for the rest of the incident.
events.note: 'shortly after the attack team reached the 11th floor'; time not given

events.text: Crews at the locked, blistering West stair door on 22; handline from the 21st-floor outlet through the wire-glass window; door forced after several minutes; cannot advance (heat, <60 psi).
Entry on 21; fire visible above through the open convenience stair; occupant hose dry; standpipe line too weak. Tactical command post on 21, staging on 20.
Fire dropping to 21 through the convenience stair (present at arrival).
Fire visible from several windows on 22; flames lap the facade; 23 subject to autoexposure. Additional alarms.
Within the next hour the fire spreads to 23 and 24, primarily by autoexposure; crews cannot enter these floors. Five-alarm assignment.
events.note: the report gives 'during the next hour' after the initial attack; 21:40 is the midpoint of that hour

events.text: Engine 11 (3) sent up the Center stair to vent at the roof; leave the stair disoriented, radio '30th floor', 'captain is down'.
Search for Engine 11 begins; helicopter roof team; an eight-member search team nearly lost in the 38th-floor mechanical room.
Helicopter searchlight finds a broken window at the SE corner of 28.
The three Engine 11 members found dead just inside the broken window on 28 (smoke inhalation; 28 not burning, heavy smoke).
Fire burning on 24 and 25 and extending to 26.
First 5-inch supply line up the West stair operational at the 24th-floor level, 'approximately six hours into the fire'.
12th alarm; second 5-inch line in the Center stair.
Third 5-inch line ordered up the East stair.
East stair line abandoned at 17. During the 5-inch work a sprinkler contractor adjusts the PRVs; normal handline streams at last, but several floors are involved.
After almost 11 hours, interior firefighting halted (collapse risk); evacuation ordered. 22-24 appear under control, 25 and 26 burning and spreading upward, heavy smoke on most upper floors.
Evacuation complete; only exterior master streams from neighbouring buildings from now on.
Fire reaches 27, 28, 29 and penetrates 30 at several points (floor assembly and autoexposure); 10 sprinkler heads on 30 operate and stop it. Time not stated by the report.
Fire declared under control (February 24).

outcome.stoppedBy: 10 sprinkler heads on the fully sprinklered 30th floor, supplied by fire department pumpers

commanderKnowledge.why: nobody has called the fire department
guard says 22; fire at one window (p. 8)
flames lapping the facade to 23 and 24 within the hour (p. 9-10)
burning on 24 and 25, extending to 26 at 02:15 (p. 11); 22-23 no longer reported burning
22-24 appear under control, 25 and 26 burning and spreading upward at 07:00 (p. 11)
exterior observation only after the evacuation; the fire climbs to 30 (p. 12); time not stated, midpoint assumed

$commanderKnowledgeNote: The human-commander baseline's belief: at minute m the floors the incident commander reported as burning, from windows, crews and the guard (src/incident/commander.ts). It sees no sensor. Floors map to the office zones (row A) of the plan.

building staff: guard says 22 at arrival (minute 8)
exterior observation: windows showing fire (one at minute 8, several by ~minute 40, floors 23-24 by ~minute 80)
crew reports from the stairs and floors 20-21 (tactical command post on 21)
no elevators, no lights, no building power after ~minute 20
